title: The Bosphorus Brief — 27 September 2026
overview: A quiet Sunday for domestic Turkish news, overshadowed by the regional standoff over Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. Closer to home, a court ruling on undocumented workers' rights and a fresh reminder to keep ikamet paperwork current are the practical stories worth your attention today.

sections.heading: Iran-US Standoff: Watch, Don't Worry Yet
sections.body: Trump has rejected a new Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, part of an ongoing back-and-forth reported across state media, international, and independent outlets alike. WSJ and CNBC report Trump expects renewed bombing after the US midterms, while Iran says it is awaiting a mediated response. For residents in Türkiye, there's no direct disruption yet — Türkiye's own US travel advisory sits steady at Level 2 — but it's worth watching shipping and oil-price effects if the situation escalates, given regional economic ties.

sections.heading: Legal Win for Undocumented Workers
sections.body: An appeals court has ruled that a worker employed without formal registration can still file a service ascertainment lawsuit — a legal route to establish work history and back social security contributions even without a proper contract. This matters for foreign residents working informally: it confirms that lack of paperwork on an employer's part doesn't erase your right to pursue recognition of time worked, which can affect pensions and benefits later.

sections.heading: Ikamet Checks Continue
sections.body: Nationwide inspections in Cyprus/Kıbrıs turned up six people without valid residence permits, who were arrested. A routine but useful reminder: keep ikamet renewals current and carry your documents, especially as authorities continue periodic checks. Separately, Montenegro has announced it will end visa-free travel arrangements with Türkiye, Russia and Belarus — a development worth noting if you hold Turkish citizenship and travel that way, though no timeline was given.

sections.heading: Economy and Diplomacy Notes
sections.body: The Turkish lira sits at roughly 48.9 to the dollar and 55.8 to the euro. The OECD forecasts Turkish inflation will stay elevated for longer than earlier hoped, and the central bank's reserves dropped $4.3 billion amid what opposition-leaning outlets describe as fund market turmoil — worth watching if you hold TRY savings. On the diplomatic front, Erdoğan reiterated a message of national stability, and Foreign Minister Fidan addressed the UN General Assembly, with state media emphasizing Türkiye's stance on Palestine and its push for dialogue over conflict.

closing: Stay dry, keep your paperwork handy, and here's to a calm week ahead — çayınız sıcak olsun.
